body:
Hi David,

I have completed a further refinement and released a new exact certificate:

https://github.com/lollipoll/certified-square-packing-68/releases/tag/v1.1.0

The new certified side is exactly:

**8.798795237218283902576680967021394083521019030227879263240370**

A shorter upward-rounded bound is **s(68) ≤ 8.798795237218283903**. This improves my earlier certified side 8.798795237221 by approximately **2.716097423319033 × 10⁻¹²**.

The source comparison identifies the tighter contact branch in Francisco Couzo's earlier public coordinates. Please retain that attribution, together with Jake Loyd and the earlier contributors to this packing family. This submission provides a tighter certified refinement and analytic description; I am not claiming discovery priority for a new arrangement.

Three separately written exact geometry implementations passed all 68 unit squares, containment, and **2,278 unordered pairs**, with **zero acceptance tolerance**. The release also includes a rigorous enclosure of the selected contact-system root and exact bounds for explicitly restricted families. Unrestricted local and global optimality remain unproved.

The attached verification ZIP is self-contained. To reproduce from the repository using normal Python 3.9 or newer:

```bash
git clone --branch v1.1.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/lollipoll/certified-square-packing-68.git
cd certified-square-packing-68/refinement-v1.1.0
python3 check_hashes.py
python3 -B verify.py n68.json --n 68 --reference-side 8.798795237221
python3 -B independent_support_check.py n68.json --n 68
python3 -B verify_analytic.py
```

The authoritative certificate's SHA-256 is:

```text
6d4f72debae83b5825e91f7b090e0cee08851ad7b85400343c0dee52f468dff9
```

The rational certificate supplies the feasible packing bound. Its side is approximately 4.58039 × 10⁻⁶¹ above the enclosed contact-system side; I am not claiming that the unrounded algebraic root itself has been certified against all packing inequalities.

Could you review this updated certificate for the table and advise how the refinement should be attributed in light of the earlier submissions?

Thank you,
Seth Rehwaldt
